units.translation: 11 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) ῥυμβόνας: IV 144. ῥυμβόνες are the coilings and movements of the spiral (B, πείρας A), as it were the cup-like (A, curved B) bends. ἀζαλέας the hard (A, dry B). sch. I 1134/39 b with similar passages.
12 σπείρας εἱλήσεις in Sm
13 the other witnesses read: σὲ τὸν αὐτοφυῆ τὸν ἐν αἰθερίῳ ῥύμβῳ πάντων, from which it is clear that θεῶν is a gloss added to the last word
16 οὕτω (scil. ῥυμβόνας) — κινήσεις are read after καλεῖται, transposed by W 63
b. ἀζαλέῃσιν ἐπηρεφέας φολίδεσσιν: covered with dry scales. Lm (P)
19 εἴσατο in F : -ετο in P, L in context
145. εἴσατο: rushed. LgP
147. θέλξαι instead of κοιμίσαι. LmP
20 γρ. prefixed to the lemma in L, cf. W 52
148 a. χθονίην: as also dwelling under the earth. εὐαντέα: the easily entreated and easily propitiated or easily met.
21 χθονίην in P : νυκτιπόλον in L
b. 〈εύαντέα:〉 easy to meet. Lg
150-51 a. οἴμῃ θελγόμενος: subdued by the song. LgP
b. ἀνελύετ’ ἄκανθ〈αν〉: the bones of snakes are called ἄκανθαι. γηγενέος is taken in common, as also other reptiles 〈...〉.
26 lacuna indicated by W, you might supply something like γηγενῆ ἐστιν
155. περιπτύξαι: to embrace. LgP

156-66 a. ἡ δέ μιν ἀρκέυθ〈οιο〉: in these and the following lines he says that Medea, sprinkling the drug with juniper, put the dragon to sleep by chanting, and thus took the fleece and both departed to the ship while the beast slept, in agreement with Antimachus (fg 10 B. II 291). And Pherecydes says in the seventh book (3 fg 31 J.) that the dragon was killed by Jason. The juniper is a thorny tree, sacred to Apollo, as is recorded in the third book of the works attributed to Musaeus (2 B 2 Diels-Kranz).

7 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) ἄρκευθος: a thorny plant (A, a kind of thorny plant B), whose smell all reptiles avoid. From ἀρά, which is harm (ὅ — βλ. A, om. B), and κεύθειν: the one that hides harm, ἀράκευθος and ἄρκευθος. Or because it has hidden thorns. As in IV 156. Apollonius (οἷον sqq. A, om. B). Et. Gud. 197, 21 De Stef. sch. Theocr. I 133 b. c
3 φησι in F : φασι τὸ φάρμ. in P 6 〈... δὲ〉 καὶ Φερεκύδης Wil. ad l.
8 ἱερόν for ἴδιον Platt
b. νήριτος: much. LgP
c. πολυπρέμνοιο: many-stemmed. Lg (P)
12 167. Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) διχομήνιδα: IV 167. διχομήνιδα the fifteenth
168. 〈ἐξανέχουσαν:〉 rising. Lg
175 a. ἀγρῶσται: the hunters; it is derived from the verb ἀγρώσσω. Homer (ε 53): 'ἰχθὺς ἀγρώσσων πυκινὰ πτερὰ δεύεται ἅλμῃ.'
13 Etymologicum Magnum 14, 12 ἀγρῶται: the hunters, from ἀγρώσσω
b. ἀχαιϊνέην: Achaea is a city of Crete, in which are born deer called Achaean. 〈...〉 and the deer called σπαθῖναι, and those with large horns are called κεράσται.
